clue.text: Complain about a bone being genetically modified on account of domestic appliance

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for complain is wrapped round the rest

parts.note: to complain is to whine
the shin is the bone at the front of the lower leg

explanation.surface: Someone moans that a bone has been genetically tampered with because of some household gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'about' splits the complaint word after its first letter; 'on' and 'of' are only link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A washing machine is a typical household appliance for laundering clothes.

clue.text: At least three compositions in the Midlands

parts.note: works means compositions, at least two of them
op, for opus, is one more composition

explanation.surface: Someone has written at least three pieces somewhere in central England.
explanation.walkthrough: WORKS (two or more) plus OP (one more) makes at least three. Worksop is a town in Nottinghamshire, in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Worksop is a market town located in the East Midlands of England.

clue.text: Romans in a show with little state

indicators.note: putting on a show rearranges the letters into a new display

explanation.surface: Romans appear in a show alongside a tiny country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' rearranges the letters of ROMANS IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny republic surrounded by Italy.

clue.text: Merchant's partner, boy unknown, with tooth?

parts.note: Ivor is a boy's name
Y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A trader's associate, a lad of uncertain identity, has a tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: James Ivory was film producer Ismail Merchant's partner in Merchant Ivory Productions.
explanation.definitionFit: James Ivory partnered Ismail Merchant in films; ivory is also what tusks, large teeth, are made of.

clue.text: Harold was a man that was sponsored without success

indicators.note: without means outside, so the sponsored man goes round success

parts.note: a godson is sponsored at baptism by a godparent
a win is a success

explanation.surface: Harold was backed by a patron but never succeeded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here means outside. Harold Godwinson was King Harold II, killed at Hastings in 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Godwinson is the family name of Harold, the last Anglo-Saxon king of England.

clue.text: See 1
Be affected by meat that isn't?

definitions.meaning: to walk or speak in a dainty, affected way
the sweet filling of Christmas pies, named for meat but now made of dried fruit

explanation.definitionFit: To mince is to act affectedly; mincemeat in pies contains fruit, not meat.

clue.text: 27 28 provider to woo with golden music-maker covering rows with bird

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: covering means the instrument's letters go around the rest

parts.note: a lute is a stringed instrument
rows in the sense of noisy quarrels are dins
a tit is a small bird

explanation.surface: A gallery owner woos with a golden instrument that covers rows of birds.
explanation.walkthrough: '27 28' points to the answer of 27 across. 'covering' makes the instrument enclose the rows and the bird. The Courtauld Institute in London has a famous art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: The Courtauld Institute of Art in London runs a well-known gallery of paintings.

clue.text: Unknown at home with tooth

parts.note: in means at home
a cog is a tooth on a gear wheel

explanation.surface: Someone stays home anonymously with toothache.
explanation.walkthrough: INCOG is short for incognito.
explanation.definitionFit: Incog, short for incognito, means in disguise and unrecognised.

clue.text: Railway and road not ending at studios

parts.note: an el is an elevated railway, American style

indicators.note: not ending means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a street is a road

explanation.surface: A railway and a road stop short of the film studios.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not ending' drops the last T of STREET. Elstree is a town north of London famous for its film studios.
explanation.definitionFit: Elstree is home to major British film and television studios.

clue.text: Percussionist circles

parts.note: a ring is a circle
the letter O is circle-shaped

explanation.walkthrough: One word gives two circles here: RING and the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringo Starr was the Beatles' drummer, so the name stands for a famous percussionist.

clue.text: Speaks ill of dental exchange for 10 oz.

indicators.note: T and D are both dental consonants, so swapping one for the other is a dental exchange

parts.note: 10 oz is ten ounces, oz being the abbreviation for ounce

explanation.surface: A dentist's swap is described as being worth ten ounces, and someone badmouths it.
explanation.walkthrough: Write 10 oz out as TEN OUNCES, then 'dental exchange for' swaps the T for D, the other consonant made with the tongue on the teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce someone is to condemn them publicly, which is to speak ill of them.

clue.text: Disreputable aspect of setter in 23 across?

parts.note: the setter standing on his own side of the sea at the shore of the other clue

explanation.surface: The crossword setter's seedy side shows at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 across is COASTLINE, where land meets sea; the setter there is on 'my side' of the SEA.
explanation.definitionFit: The seamy side of something is its sordid, unpleasant aspect.

clue.text: See 24
Religious official's reasoning in case of A1

indicators.note: the word for reasoning, cased in A and 1, loses that case to leave the official

parts.note: a priori reasoning argues from causes to effects
A and 1, the numeral 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A churchman's logic is found in a first-class case.
explanation.walkthrough: A PRIORI reasoning is the official set in a case made of A and I (1 read as I); take the case away and the official remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A prior is the head of a priory, a religious house, so a monastic official.

clue.text: Hercule II, revolutionary French churchman

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A second Hercule turns out to be a rebel French cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' rearranges HERCULE II, with II as two letter I's. Cardinal Richelieu was chief minister of Louis XIII.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal Richelieu was a powerful French cardinal and statesman.

clue.text: Vehicle, back number -put in petrol that's not yet tried?

indicators.note: back says the vehicle's word is read from the end to the start

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle

indicators.note: the number is put in the word for petrol

parts.note: juice is slang for fuel such as petrol
D is 500 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Some vehicle gets a number added to its fuel, a matter not yet tested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reads the vehicle backwards and 'put in' places the Roman numeral inside the fuel word; D for 500 is a standard crossword number.
explanation.definitionFit: Sub judice, Latin for under a judge, describes a case before the courts and not yet decided.

clue.text: Improper delivery arising in large pool

indicators.note: in means the reversed piece goes inside the word for large

parts.note: big means large

indicators.note: arising in a down clue means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a no-ball is an illegal delivery by a bowler in cricket

explanation.surface: A badly bowled ball comes up in a big swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a no-ball is an illegal delivery. 'arising' turns NOBALL into LLABON, and 'in' puts it in BIG.
explanation.definitionFit: A billabong is an Australian pool or backwater left by a river.

clue.text: See 6
Another cartoon by a student in dentistry

indicators.note: another version of the word cartoon is a rearrangement of its letters

parts.note: L is a learner, the plate on a student driver's car

explanation.surface: A dental student draws yet another cartoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' signals rearranging the word cartoon; 'by' simply joins on the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A root canal is a dental procedure, so the phrase belongs to dentistry.

clue.text: It's all up with poor horse being grabbed by inhuman lawman

indicators.note: in a down clue all up means the whole thing is read upwards, backwards
the horse is grabbed and held inside the word for poor

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy horse

explanation.surface: A robot policeman grabs a sorry nag and it is all over for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being grabbed by' encloses the horse; 'It's all up with' then reverses the whole, as a down clue reads upward. RoboCop is the cyborg policeman of the 1987 film.
explanation.definitionFit: RoboCop is a cyborg police officer, part machine and so not human.

clue.text: Find very abstracted jockey's field

indicators.note: abstracted means taken away, so letters from very are removed

parts.note: to find is to discover
very cut short to its first three letters

explanation.surface: Something is found, very absent-mindedly, in a rider's patch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abstracted' takes VER (the start of 'very') out of DISCOVER. The 'jockey' is a disc jockey, not a horse rider.
explanation.definitionFit: Disco is the kind of music a disc jockey plays, so it is the DJ's domain.

clue.text: When anyone can see the goal with love and money around

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: around means the money word goes around the goal

parts.note: pay is money earned
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: Anyone can watch the goal while love and cash circulate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' makes the money word enclose the goal; the love comes first in the answer even though the clue names it later.
explanation.definitionFit: An open day is when an institution lets the public in to look round.

clue.text: Robin's partner, perhaps, to have a dip

parts.note: Batman is Robin's crime-fighting partner, read as bat plus man
the man half of Batman is a he

explanation.surface: Batman, perhaps, goes for a swim.
explanation.walkthrough: Batman is bat plus man, and a man is a he: the clue rewrites the hero's name rather than defining it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe is to swim or take a dip in water.

clue.text: Subject to choice when king departs

indicators.note: the king departing means his letter leaves the word

parts.note: a pick is a choice
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: A matter is up for choice once the king has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'departs' takes K off PICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a subject of discussion.

clue.text: Incline to install oven at Land's End?

indicators.note: to install is to put something inside, so the oven goes in

parts.note: a cline is a gradient or slope
an oast is a kiln for drying hops

explanation.surface: Someone tends to fit a stove at the far tip of Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is England's westernmost point, in Cornwall; read as the end of the land it means the shore. An OAST is a hop-drying kiln, common in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: The coastline is where land ends and sea begins.

clue.text: Many suffer in hidey-hole

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
to ache is to suffer pain

explanation.surface: Lots of people suffer while hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden store or hiding place.

clue.text: Rebel to get endless military provision

indicators.note: provision, read as an arrangement, rearranges the letters
endless means the last letter is cut off

explanation.surface: A rebel acquires endless army supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the Y of MILITARY; 'provision' rearranges MILITAR with GET. The Tamil Tigers were a Sri Lankan separatist group.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tamil Tiger was a member of a Sri Lankan rebel separatist movement.

clue.text: Lively piece for island company around Jersey etc

parts.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples

indicators.note: around means the company's letters go round the islands

parts.note: CI stands for the Channel Islands, which include Jersey

explanation.surface: A lively composition is written for an island firm working round the Channel Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey and Guernsey are the Channel Islands, abbreviated CI.
explanation.definitionFit: A capriccio is a lively, free-form piece of music.

clue.text: Off form?

parts.note: the shape or growth taken by food that has gone off, and also a shaping form

explanation.definitionFit: A mould is both a form for shaping and the fungus that grows on food gone off.

clue.text: One caught entering clean kitchen without right, a hanging matter?

indicators.note: entering means going inside the word for clean

parts.note: pure means clean
I is the Roman numeral one
CT is a scorecard abbreviation for caught in cricket

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the kitchen goes round right

parts.note: a galley is a ship's kitchen

explanation.surface: Someone is caught breaking into a spotless kitchen, a crime that might once have earned the noose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts the one and the catch inside clean; 'without' means outside, the kitchen round right. Hanged pictures make the definition a pun on the gallows.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture gallery is where pictures are hung, so it is literally a hanging matter.

clue.text: See 27
